thread:
jordan: Hey team — presales handoff for the Zenith POC. They want reserved capacity + autoscale. Key asks: 200 steady qps, 400 avg tokens per request, 10k concurrent users anticipated during peak campaigns (~2m tokens/min). HIPAA + SSO via Okta, KMS for keys. Can we sketch a provisioning plan and any enterprise blockers?

mia (Solutions Eng): Quick calc first: 200 qps * 400 tokens = 80k tokens/sec steady. Peak campaign 1k qps => 400k tokens/sec short bursts. Need to translate tokens/sec to GPU throughput (depends on model/quantization). Which model are they targeting?

jordan: They're evaluating a quantized Llama variant (7B Q4). Preference for our dedicated pool with reserved GPUs. Also asked about preheat windows and KV warmup time.

sam (Sales Eng): For 7B Q4 on A100-equivalent, rough baseline: ~30-45k tokens/sec per GPU for gen-heavy loads (short context). For longer contexts throughput drops. I'd recommend reserving 8 GPUs for steady headroom, with autoscale target +4 GPUs for burst to cover ~1.5x peak while we test.

david (SRE): Notes on autoscale policies: use target_cpu_tokens or target_qps policy. For this workload I suggest policy by inflight requests and KV cache hit ratio. Also add a prewarm hook: on canary -> run kv_warmup job. Autoscale cooldowns should be 90s min to avoid thrash.

mia (Solutions Eng): Practical plan:
- Reserve: 8 gpus (us-west-2)
- Autoscale: max 12 gpus, min 6 gpus for maintenance window tolerance
- Preheat: schedule 15m before campaign start + run synthetic KV warmup (script below)

KV warmup snippet:
```bash
redwoodctl kv-warmup --model=llama-7b-q4 --shards=8 --duration=900
```

That will populate prefixes and reduce tail latency.

jordan: Good. Any compliance blockers for HIPAA + KMS + SSO?

legal-ops: HIPAA requires isolated tenancy and audit logs. Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC + customer-managed KMS is fine. We need a Data Processing Agreement + BAA. Ask customer for data flow diagram. Okta SAML + SCIM provisioning supported.

david (SRE): Operational caveats: if they plan cross-AZ traffic, ensure model replicas pinned per-AZ for locality. Fallback policy: if reserved pool is full, route to quantized cheap variant (llama-7b-q4f32) and degrade gracefully. Add routing rule in config:
```yaml
routing: 
  - preferred: reserved-llama-7b-q4
  - fallback: quant-7b-q4f32
  - max_latency_ms: 450
```

sam (Sales Eng): Pricing Qs: Jordan — they asked about cost impact of reserve vs burst credits. Prepare two sketches: committed monthly (8 GPUs) and burst unit pricing per additional GPU-minute. I can pull numbers but need expected campaign duration (hours per week).
jordan: Campaigns are ~3 hours/day for 2 weeks, then steady background traffic rest of month.

mia (Solutions Eng): For sizing runbook:
1) Preflight smoke: run synthetic at 1.2x steady for 30m.
2) KV preload: run kv-warmup 15m before go-live.
3) Monitor: token/sec, tail P99, GPU util, KV hit rate. Alert if P99 > 800ms or GPU util > 85% sustained.

ops-bot: Deploy plan created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/zenith-provision (access: sales, se, sre, legal). :white_check_mark:

david (SRE): One more: spot instances are not allowed for HIPAA workloads. Mark node pools as on-demand. Also consider AZ spread 3-way to tolerate AZ loss.

jordan: Thanks team — I'll assemble a one-page handoff for sales ops with the reserve=8 / autoscale to 12 plan, security checklist (BAA, KMS, Okta), and preheat runbook. Sam, can you draft the pricing sketch by EOD?

sam (Sales Eng): On it. I'll attach numbers and a conservative monthly commit vs burst example.

mia (Solutions Eng): I'll own the smoke test template and kv-warmup script. Posting it to the runbook now.

jordan: Great — filing this thread into the deal record. If anything else shows up (customer asks for lower latency SLOs), we may need to trade cost for more GPUs or a larger model variant.

legal-ops: I'll kick off BAA template and ask for their DPA signatures.

jordan: Closing for now. Thanks all :pray:
